passages.text: We who are strong ought to bear with the shortcomings of the weak and not to please ourselves.
passages.sermon: We who are strong must help the weak.\r\nWe must carry the burdens of those who are not strong.\r\nWe must not seek to please ourselves.
passages.original: Ὀφείλομεν δὲ ἡμεῖς οἱ δυνατοὶ τὰ ἀσθενήματα τῶν ἀδυνάτων βαστάζειν καὶ μὴ ἑαυτοῖς ἀρέσκειν

passages.text: Each of us should please his neighbor for his good, to build him up.
passages.sermon:
Each of us must act for the good of our neighbor.
We must seek to build up our neighbor.
We should not focus only on ourselves.
We must help others grow and become stronger.
We do this by doing what is good for them.
passages.original: ἕκαστος ἡμῶν τῷ πλησίον ἀρεσκέτω εἰς τὸ ἀγαθὸν πρὸς οἰκοδομήν

passages.text: For even Christ did not please Himself, but as it is written: “The insults of those who insult You have fallen on Me.”
passages.sermon:
Christ is our Lord and Savior.
Christ did not seek to please Himself.
Scripture says this about Christ.
The insults of those who insult God fell on Christ.
passages.original: καὶ γὰρ ὁ Χριστὸς οὐχ ἑαυτῷ ἤρεσεν ἀλλὰ καθὼς γέγραπται Οἱ ὀνειδισμοὶ τῶν ὀνειδιζόντων σε ἐπέπεσαν ἐπ’ ἐμέ

passages.text: For everything that was written in the past was written for our instruction, so that through endurance and the encouragement of the Scriptures, we might have hope.
passages.sermon:
God gave us the Scriptures in the past.
God caused everything written in the Scriptures to teach us.
The Scriptures give us instruction.
We learn from the Scriptures.
We gain endurance through the Scriptures.
The Scriptures encourage us.
The Scriptures help us to have hope.
passages.original: ὅσα γὰρ προεγράφη πάντα εἰς τὴν ἡμετέραν διδασκαλίαν ἐγράφη ἵνα διὰ τῆς ὑπομονῆς καὶ διὰ τῆς παρακλήσεως τῶν γραφῶν τὴν ἐλπίδα ἔχωμεν

passages.text: Now may the God who gives endurance and encouragement grant you harmony with one another in Christ Jesus, so that with one mind and one voice you may glorify the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ.
passages.sermon:
God gives endurance.
God gives encouragement.
I pray that God will help you think the same way toward each other.
You must do this because you belong to Christ Jesus.
When you are united in mind and voice, you can glorify God.
God is the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ.
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ Θεὸς τῆς ὑπομονῆς καὶ τῆς παρακλήσεως δῴη ὑμῖν τὸ αὐτὸ φρονεῖν ἐν ἀλλήλοις κατὰ Χριστὸν Ἰησοῦν ἵνα ὁμοθυμαδὸν ἐν ἑνὶ στόματι δοξάζητε τὸν Θεὸν καὶ Πατέρα τοῦ Κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ

passages.text: Accept one another, then, just as Christ accepted you, in order to bring glory to God.
passages.sermon:
Christ accepted you.
Christ did this to bring glory to God.
Therefore, accept one another.
When you accept one another, you also bring glory to God.
passages.original: Διὸ προσλαμβάνεσθε ἀλλήλους καθὼς καὶ ὁ Χριστὸς προσελάβετο ὑμᾶς εἰς δόξαν τοῦ Θεοῦ

passages.text: For I tell you that Christ has become a servant of the circumcised on behalf of God’s truth, to confirm the promises made to the patriarchs, so that the Gentiles may glorify God for His mercy. As it is written: “Therefore I will praise You among the Gentiles; I will sing hymns to Your name.”
passages.sermon:
Christ became a servant to the circumcised.
The circumcised are the Jews.
Christ served them for the sake of God’s truth.
He did this to confirm the promises God made to the patriarchs.
The patriarchs are the ancestors of the Jewish people.
Christ also acted so that the Gentiles may glorify God.
The Gentiles are all other nations.
The Gentiles glorify God because of His mercy.
It is written:
“Therefore I will praise You among the Gentiles.
I will sing hymns to Your name.”
passages.original: λέγω γὰρ Χριστὸν διάκονον γεγενῆσθαι περιτομῆς ὑπὲρ ἀληθείας Θεοῦ εἰς τὸ βεβαιῶσαι τὰς ἐπαγγελίας τῶν πατέρων τὰ δὲ ἔθνη ὑπὲρ ἐλέους δοξάσαι τὸν Θεόν καθὼς γέγραπται Διὰ τοῦτο ἐξομολογήσομαί σοι ἐν ἔθνεσιν καὶ τῷ ὀνόματί σου ψαλῶ

passages.text: Again, it says: “Rejoice, O Gentiles, with His people.”
passages.sermon:
Paul writes to the church in Rome.
Paul teaches both Jews and Gentiles.
Paul quotes the Scriptures.
The Scriptures say, “Rejoice, O Gentiles, with His people.”
God calls the Gentiles to rejoice.
God calls the Gentiles to join His people in joy.
passages.original: Καὶ πάλιν λέγει Εὐφράνθητε ἔθνη μετὰ τοῦ λαοῦ αὐτοῦ

passages.text: And again: “Praise the Lord, all you Gentiles, and extol Him, all you peoples.”
passages.sermon: All Gentiles must praise the Lord.\r\nAll peoples must extol Him.
passages.original: Καὶ πάλιν Αἰνεῖτε πάντα τὰ ἔθνη τὸν Κύριον καὶ ἐπαινεσάτωσαν αὐτὸν πάντες οἱ λαοί

passages.text: And once more, Isaiah says: “The Root of Jesse will appear, One who will arise to rule over the Gentiles; in Him the Gentiles will put their hope.”
passages.sermon:
Isaiah was a prophet.
Isaiah spoke about the future.
Isaiah said, “The Root of Jesse will appear.”
Jesse was the father of King David.
The Root of Jesse means a descendant from Jesse’s family.
This descendant will come.
He will rise up to rule over the Gentiles.
The Gentiles are all the nations who are not Jews.
The Gentiles will put their hope in Him.
This descendant is the one in whom the nations trust.
passages.original: Καὶ πάλιν Ἠσαΐας λέγει Ἔσται ἡ ῥίζα τοῦ Ἰεσσαί καὶ ὁ ἀνιστάμενος ἄρχειν ἐθνῶν ἐπ’ αὐτῷ ἔθνη ἐλπιοῦσιν

passages.text: Now may the God of hope fill you with all joy and peace as you believe in Him, so that you may overflow with hope by the power of the Holy Spirit.
passages.sermon:
God gives hope.
God can fill you with joy.
God can fill you with peace.
You receive this as you believe in Him.
God wants you to overflow with hope.
The Holy Spirit gives you this power.
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ Θεὸς τῆς ἐλπίδος πληρώσαι ὑμᾶς πάσης χαρᾶς καὶ εἰρήνης ἐν τῷ πιστεύειν εἰς τὸ περισσεύειν ὑμᾶς ἐν τῇ ἐλπίδι ἐν δυνάμει Πνεύματος Ἁγίου

passages.text: I myself am convinced, my brothers, that you yourselves are full of goodness, brimming with knowledge, and able to instruct one another.
passages.sermon:
Paul writes to the believers in Rome.
Paul calls them his brothers.
Paul says he is convinced about them.
Paul believes they are full of goodness.
Paul believes they are filled with all knowledge.
Paul says they are able to instruct one another.
passages.original: Πέπεισμαι δέ ἀδελφοί μου καὶ αὐτὸς ἐγὼ περὶ ὑμῶν ὅτι καὶ αὐτοὶ μεστοί ἐστε ἀγαθωσύνης πεπληρωμένοι πάσης τῆς γνώσεως δυνάμενοι καὶ ἀλλήλους νουθετεῖν

passages.text: However, I have written you a bold reminder on some points, because of the grace God has given me to be a minister of Christ Jesus to the Gentiles in the priestly service of the gospel of God, so that the Gentiles might become an offering acceptable to God, sanctified by the Holy Spirit.
passages.sermon:
God gave me grace.
God made me a minister of Christ Jesus.
God sent me to serve the Gentiles.
I serve by sharing the gospel of God.
I wrote to you boldly on some points.
I wanted to remind you.
I do this so the Gentiles may become an offering to God.
God accepts this offering.
The Holy Spirit makes this offering holy.
passages.original: τολμηρότερον δὲ ἔγραψα ὑμῖν ἀπὸ μέρους ὡς ἐπαναμιμνήσκων ὑμᾶς διὰ τὴν χάριν τὴν δοθεῖσάν μοι ὑπὸ τοῦ Θεοῦ εἰς τὸ εἶναί με λειτουργὸν Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ εἰς τὰ ἔθνη ἱερουργοῦντα τὸ εὐαγγέλιον τοῦ Θεοῦ ἵνα γένηται ἡ προσφορὰ τῶν ἐθνῶν εὐπρόσδεκτος ἡγιασμένη ἐν Πνεύματι Ἁγίῳ

passages.text: Therefore I exult in Christ Jesus in my service to God.
passages.sermon:
Paul is an apostle of Jesus Christ.
Paul serves God.
Paul rejoices in Christ Jesus.
Paul finds his pride in Christ Jesus.
Paul boasts about his work for God through Christ Jesus.
passages.original: Ἔχω οὖν τὴν καύχησιν ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ τὰ πρὸς τὸν Θεόν

passages.text: I will not presume to speak of anything except what Christ has accomplished through me in leading the Gentiles to obedience by word and deed, by the power of signs and wonders, and by the power of the Spirit of God. So from Jerusalem all the way around to Illyricum, I have fully proclaimed the gospel of Christ.
passages.sermon:
Paul is a minister of Christ Jesus to the Gentiles.
Paul will not speak about anything except what Christ has done through him.
Christ has worked through Paul to lead the Gentiles to obey God.
Christ has done this through Paul's words and actions.
Christ has shown power through signs and wonders.
Christ has worked by the power of the Spirit of God.
Paul has fully proclaimed the gospel of Christ.
Paul has done this from Jerusalem all the way around to Illyricum.
passages.original: οὐ γὰρ τολμήσω τι λαλεῖν ὧν οὐ κατειργάσατο Χριστὸς δι’ ἐμοῦ εἰς ὑπακοὴν ἐθνῶν λόγῳ καὶ ἔργῳ ἐν δυνάμει σημείων καὶ τεράτων ἐν δυνάμει Πνεύματος θεοῦ ὥστε με ἀπὸ Ἰερουσαλὴμ καὶ κύκλῳ μέχρι τοῦ Ἰλλυρικοῦ πεπληρωκέναι τὸ εὐαγγέλιον τοῦ Χριστοῦ

passages.text: In this way I have aspired to preach the gospel where Christ was not known, so that I would not be building on someone else’s foundation.
passages.sermon:
Paul is an apostle of Jesus Christ.
Paul wants to preach the gospel.
Paul chooses places where people do not know Christ.
Paul does not preach where Christ is already known.
Paul does not want to build on someone else’s foundation.
passages.original: οὕτως δὲ φιλοτιμούμενον εὐαγγελίζεσθαι οὐχ ὅπου ὠνομάσθη Χριστός ἵνα μὴ ἐπ’ ἀλλότριον θεμέλιον οἰκοδομῶ

passages.text: Rather, as it is written: “Those who were not told about Him will see, and those who have not heard will understand.”
passages.sermon:
Scripture says this.
Some people have not been told about Christ.
These people will see Him.
Some people have not heard about Christ.
These people will understand.
passages.original: ἀλλὰ καθὼς γέγραπται Ὄψονται οἷς οὐκ ἀνηγγέλη περὶ αὐτοῦ καὶ οἳ οὐκ ἀκηκόασιν συνήσουσιν

passages.text: That is why I have often been hindered from coming to you.
passages.sermon:
Paul is the writer.
Paul wanted to visit the believers in Rome.
Paul often could not come to them.
Paul was hindered many times from coming to them.
Paul’s work in preaching the gospel kept him away.
passages.original: Διὸ καὶ ἐνεκοπτόμην τὰ πολλὰ τοῦ ἐλθεῖν πρὸς ὑμᾶς

passages.text: But now that there are no further opportunities for me in these regions, and since I have longed for many years to visit you, I hope to see you on my way to Spain. And after I have enjoyed your company for a while, you can equip me for my journey.
passages.sermon:
Paul is writing to the believers in Rome.
Paul has finished his work in these regions.
Paul has no more opportunities to serve here.
Paul has wanted to visit the believers in Rome for many years.
Paul hopes to see them as he travels to Spain.
Paul wants to spend some time with them.
Paul hopes they will help him on his journey to Spain after he visits them.
passages.original: Νυνὶ δὲ μηκέτι τόπον ἔχων ἐν τοῖς κλίμασι τούτοις ἐπιποθίαν δὲ ἔχων τοῦ ἐλθεῖν πρὸς ὑμᾶς ἀπὸ ἱκανῶν ἐτῶν ὡς ἂν πορεύωμαι εἰς τὴν Σπανίαν ἐλπίζω γὰρ διαπορευόμενος θεάσασθαι ὑμᾶς καὶ ὑφ’ ὑμῶν προπεμφθῆναι ἐκεῖ ἐὰν ὑμῶν πρῶτον ἀπὸ μέρους ἐμπλησθῶ

passages.text: Now, however, I am on my way to Jerusalem to serve the saints there.
passages.sermon:
Paul is now traveling to Jerusalem.
He is going to serve the saints there.
The saints are the believers in Jerusalem.
Paul’s purpose is to help them.
passages.original: Νυνὶ δὲ πορεύομαι εἰς Ἰερουσαλὴμ διακονῶν τοῖς ἁγίοις

passages.text: For Macedonia and Achaia were pleased to make a contribution for the poor among the saints in Jerusalem.
passages.sermon:
Macedonia and Achaia are Christian regions.
The people in Macedonia and Achaia decided to help others.
They wanted to give a gift.
They chose to give this gift to the poor.
These poor people are believers in Jerusalem.
Macedonia and Achaia were happy to make this contribution.
passages.original: εὐδόκησαν γὰρ Μακεδονία καὶ Ἀχαΐα κοινωνίαν τινὰ ποιήσασθαι εἰς τοὺς πτωχοὺς τῶν ἁγίων τῶν ἐν Ἰερουσαλήμ

passages.text: They were pleased to do it, and indeed they owe it to them. For if the Gentiles have shared in their spiritual blessings, they are obligated to minister to them with material blessings.
passages.sermon:
The believers in Macedonia and Achaia gave a gift to the poor saints in Jerusalem.
They were happy to give this gift.
They also owed this help to the saints in Jerusalem.
The Gentiles received spiritual blessings from the Jewish believers in Jerusalem.
Because of this, the Gentiles must help the Jewish believers with material things.
passages.original: εὐδόκησαν γάρ καὶ ὀφειλέται εἰσὶν αὐτῶν εἰ γὰρ τοῖς πνευματικοῖς αὐτῶν ἐκοινώνησαν τὰ ἔθνη ὀφείλουσιν καὶ ἐν τοῖς σαρκικοῖς λειτουργῆσαι αὐτοῖς

passages.text: So after I have completed this service and have safely delivered this bounty to them, I will set off to Spain by way of you.
passages.sermon:
Paul is the speaker.
\r\nPaul serves the saints in Jerusalem.
\r\nPaul collects a gift for the poor among the saints in Jerusalem.
\r\nPaul plans to finish this service.
\r\nPaul will deliver this gift to the saints in Jerusalem.
\r\nPaul will make sure the saints receive the gift.
\r\nAfter Paul completes this task, he will travel to Spain.
\r\nPaul will go to Spain by way of the believers he addresses.
passages.original: Τοῦτο οὖν ἐπιτελέσας καὶ σφραγισάμενος αὐτοῖς τὸν καρπὸν τοῦτον ἀπελεύσομαι δι’ ὑμῶν εἰς Σπανίαν

passages.text: I know that when I come to you, I will come in the fullness of the blessing of Christ.
passages.sermon:
Paul is the writer of this letter.
Paul is an apostle of Jesus Christ.
Paul speaks to the believers in Rome.
Paul knows he will visit them.
Paul will come to them.
Paul will bring the full blessing of Christ when he comes.
passages.original: οἶδα δὲ ὅτι ἐρχόμενος πρὸς ὑμᾶς ἐν πληρώματι εὐλογίας Χριστοῦ ἐλεύσομαι

passages.text: Now I urge you, brothers, by our Lord Jesus Christ and by the love of the Spirit, to join me in my struggle by praying to God for me.
passages.sermon:
Paul writes this letter to the believers in Rome.
Paul calls them brothers.
Paul urges them to help him.
Paul urges them by our Lord Jesus Christ.
Paul urges them by the love of the Spirit.
Paul asks them to join him in his struggle.
Paul asks them to pray to God for him.
passages.original: Παρακαλῶ δὲ ὑμᾶς ἀδελφοί διὰ τοῦ Κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ καὶ διὰ τῆς ἀγάπης τοῦ Πνεύματος συναγωνίσασθαί μοι ἐν ταῖς προσευχαῖς ὑπὲρ ἐμοῦ πρὸς τὸν Θεόν

passages.text: Pray that I may be delivered from the unbelievers in Judea, and that my service in Jerusalem may be acceptable to the saints there, so that by God’s will I may come to you with joy and together with you be refreshed.
passages.sermon:
Paul is writing to the believers in Rome.
Paul asks them to pray for him.
Paul wants God to deliver him from the unbelievers in Judea.
Paul wants his service in Jerusalem to be acceptable to the saints there.
Paul desires to come to the believers in Rome with joy.
Paul wants to visit them by the will of God.
Paul hopes to be refreshed together with them.
passages.original: ἵνα ῥυσθῶ ἀπὸ τῶν ἀπειθούντων ἐν τῇ Ἰουδαίᾳ καὶ ἡ διακονία μου ἡ εἰς Ἰερουσαλὴμ εὐπρόσδεκτος τοῖς ἁγίοις γένηται ἵνα ἐν χαρᾷ ἐλθὼν πρὸς ὑμᾶς διὰ θελήματος Θεοῦ συναναπαύσωμαι ὑμῖν

passages.text: The God of peace be with all of you. Amen.
passages.sermon: God is the God of peace.\r\nGod is with all of you.\r\nAmen.
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ Θεὸς τῆς εἰρήνης μετὰ πάντων ὑμῶν ἀμήν
